# mermaid-callouts

Requires every mermaid diagram with callouts to have a callout table whose callouts match it one to one. Orphan callouts, orphan rows, and duplicates fail. It is the foundational check of the mermaid diagram and callout table fitness-function set ([#28](https://github.com/may-journal/fitness-runner/issues/28)).

## Behavior

For each `.md` file, diagrams (fenced `mermaid` blocks) are paired with the callout table that follows them. That table is a GFM table whose first header cell is `#`, `No`, `Callout`, or `Ref`.

Nodes carry number callouts and connectors carry letter callouts, so a reader tells them apart at a glance ([#583](https://github.com/may-journal/fitness-runner/issues/583)). Letters run `A` to `Z`, then double: `AA`, `BB`, up to `ZZ`, then `AAA`. The table's `#` column holds the same letters for connector rows.

- Pass: every callout in the diagram maps to exactly one table row, and vice versa. Diagrams without callouts need no table.
- Fail (orphan callout): `diagram callout N has no matching table row`.
- Fail (orphan row): `callout table row N has no matching diagram callout`.
- Fail (duplicate): `diagram callout N appears K times` or `callout table row N appears K times`.
- Fail (numbered connector): `connector callout N must be a letter; numbers are for nodes`.
- Fail (broken doubling): `connector callout AB breaks the letter doubling`, or the same for a table row. A label such as YES that no row lists is prose.
- Fail (unpaired diagram): `mermaid diagram … has callouts but no associated callout table`.
- Fail (unpaired table): `callout table … has no preceding mermaid diagram`.

## Reading callouts

A node callout is the leading integer of a node label: quoted (`Container(x, "3", …)`, `A["1 Check"]`) or inside a node shape (`A[2 Screen]`).

A connector callout is the leading label of an edge, in any of these forms:

- C4 relationship: `Rel(a, b, "A")`.
- Flowchart pipe: `a -->|B| b` or `a -->|"B"| b`.
- Inline link: `a -- C --> b`.
- Colon after an arrow: `a --> b : D` or `a ->> b: D`.

A colon label with no arrow before it, such as a state description or a note, is a node's. Capital letters that break the doubling count only when they are the whole label, so prose such as `|API calls|` is not a callout. Such a label also never makes a diagram need a table on its own. In the table, callouts come from the first (`#`) column: a number, capital letters, or either in brackets.

## Scope

Runs on every `.md` file that contains a diagram or callout table. Files with neither are skipped and don't count toward `filesChecked`.
